packageRules.description: Group all Actions bumps (github-actions manager also covers .forgejo/workflows) into one PR.

nginx + supervisor are pinned in the Dockerfile and tracked via the `deb` datasource (markers there). Repology strips the Debian -N+debNNuM revision so it can't see security rebuilds; the deb datasource reads the actual package index. Point it at both trixie (base) and trixie-security so security revisions are picked up — Renovate merges the registries and takes the highest. All apt bumps grouped into one PR.

Exempt the deb datasource from the global 3-day minimumReleaseAge. Two reasons: the debian-apt group's whole point is picking up trixie-security rebuilds, which must not wait out an age gate (and the vulnerabilityAlerts fast path can't help - that only covers GitHub's advisory DB, which has no deb coverage and is inert on the Forgejo platform anyway; osvVulnerabilityAlerts likewise has no deb coverage); and the deb datasource may not supply releaseTimestamps, which under internalChecksFilter=strict would silently freeze apt bumps forever rather than delay them.
Standalone bumps for tool versions tracked in build.yml (crane, etc.).

Major bumps require manual review — surface as checkboxes on the Dependency Dashboard, do not open the PR automatically, do not auto-merge. Minor/patch still flow through automerge gated by all-ci (which must be a required status check in the Forgejo branch protection for platformAutomerge to wait on it).

Keep workflow actions on floating major tags (@vN). Suppress pin/patch/minor so they are never pinned to an exact patch (upstream moves the @vN tag, so patch fixes land at runtime without a PR); a new MAJOR still surfaces via the rule above. Applies to both the Forgejo workflows and any remaining GitHub workflow copy.
